one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent failed to correctly implement the inverse of the decompressor's adaptive arithmetic coding integer encoding, causing persistent floating-point exceptions and segfaults across all 99 steps, and ultimately submitted a truncated non-functional compressed file.
t_err_evidence: agent writes comp.c with flawed put_integer/put_bit logic that causes floating point exception
t_commit_evidence: Step 5: The fundamental algorithmic error in put_integer is locked in from the first compressor write. All subsequent iterations (Python rewrites, different leading-zero counts, LZ additions, C variants) are variations on the same incorrect algorithm and never recover. The agent never identifies the correct inverse of the decompressor's encoding.
t_surface_evidence: Floating point exception (core dumped) when running ./comp data.txt > data.comp
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly identifies the algorithm as adaptive arithmetic coding but lacks the domain knowledge to correctly reverse the specific put_integer / get_integer design used in this decompressor. The decompressor's get_integer uses a while loop that calls get_bit at sequentially-increasing context numbers (starting from size+1) until a 1 is returned, then reads tmp more bits; the agent never correctly derives that the encoder must start with range=1 and emit enough bytes to prevent zero-division before sending any 1 bit, nor does it correctly track how the adaptive counts synchronize between encoder and decoder.
